title: Walk-On

intro.text: Midnight at the Foundry. The arena lights come up on a walk-on with no entrance music.
Breaking news, and I mean breaking. Tonight's walk-on used to run this show.
No sponsor. No record. One baton. I signed the sheet like everybody else.
You said there wasn't an exit.
There isn't. There's only the next show. Tonight, I'm on the card.
Network rules: the walk-on gets an extra stock. The champion gets top billing. Top billing is big.
Fine. Bring the baton.

outro.text: The baton spins across the floor. The arena holds its breath.
Best ratings this show has ever had. And I wasn't even hosting.
Headline: Former Host Walks On, Walks Off, Champion Stays Champion. Working title.
Keep the baton. I'll keep the card.
Same time tomorrow?
Same time tomorrow.

If the card is his, the audience is mine. Let's see how he does when the network turns up the gravity.
Three extra jumps. Best air speed on the roster. Try keeping up.
Short night. Let's go.

outro.text: Okay. That was a lot of ground.
Headline: Rival Network Loses First Round, Blames Floor. It's too long, I know.

Even speed. Even power. I've watched every one of your tapes.
Then you know how this ends.
Don't spoil the rerun.

outro.text: The tape said you'd lose that one.
The tape's wrong.
Ratings are up, and the rerun is cancelled. Mid-season, no less.
Cancelled. Fine. Live television, then.

title: Cut to Size

You didn't try to win.

Stay behind me.

tagline: The network gives the champion a lifetime award, and a quota to earn it.
hint: Quota: deal 250% before the 90-second clock runs out. Every hit lands a little harder (damage 110%). Slice is quick and keeps cutting in: stay on him, and don't wait for the clock.

intro.text: Space Chess. The board is set for a ceremony: a long table, a short speech.
Tonight the champion receives a Lifetime Achievement Award. The network asks for 250 percent of applause in ninety seconds, which in this show means damage. Slice is presenting the ribbon.
I have been cutting the ribbon all night. I have not had a chance to cut anything else.
Cut this.

outro.text: Lifetime. Already?
The champion has a lifetime award and, according to the network, a lifetime to spend it. The award is heavier than it looks.
Seems so.

title: Best in Show
tagline: The big envelope, and an editor who wants a clean acceptance.
hint: Clean streak: land 4 hits in a row without being hit back, before the 90-second clock runs out. Getting hit starts the count over. Every hit lands harder (damage 120%). Susan hits like a tax bill: poke, then back off, and don't trade.

intro.text: Humans In The Loop. The last category of the night, the biggest envelope, and a stage lit like a trophy.
Best in Show. The editor wants a clean acceptance clip: four hits in a row, no cuts, before the clock runs out. Get hit and the footage is ruined. Also, Susan has asked for a word with the champion.
I have waited since The Champion's Tax. I want the receipt.
Come and get it.

outro.text: Keep the trophy. I will keep the receipt.
The acceptance speech runs four words long, which is the first speech this season to come in under time. The network has asked for it to be longer.
Thanks. Good night. Goodbye. Nice.
Four nominees. Four envelopes. The speech was four words.

title: Teaser
tagline: Season 9 opens with thirty seconds of footage and no explanation.
hint: Gravity is a little heavy (115%): your jumps are short and you fall fast, so keep your feet near the roof and make Shark Dude come to you. 3 stocks each.

intro.text: City Top. The rooftop is dark except for a screen, and the screen is counting down.
Welcome to Season 9. The network has cut a teaser for the finale. It is thirty seconds long, it shows nothing, and it ends on a sign-up sheet.
I defended this roof once. I am here to watch the champion defend it.
Watch closer.

outro.text: Good teaser.
The footage is out. The sheet at the end of the clip has a name on it, and the network will not say whose. The ratings are up anyway.
Next clip.

title: Trailer
tagline: Two walk-ons cut a trailer together and neither will share the voiceover.
hint: Two on one: Wallit pushes with sponsor money, Cel keeps coming back for more. They have two stocks each, you have three. Take the quicker one out first.

intro.text: Rainbow Full Pipe. Two lights on the pipe, one for each walk-on.
In a world where the champion has cleared eight seasons, two walk-ons share a trailer. The voiceover has not been recorded. Neither of them will let the other do it.
This trailer is sponsored. I would like my name in the first ten seconds.
I would like my name in the first five.
Your names are fine. Fight.

outro.text: The trailer ran a minute long.
The best part was cut.
The voiceover went to the champion, who recorded four words. The network says it tests well.
Coming this fall.

title: Table Read
tagline: The cast sits down with the finale script, and every page has a hole in it.
hint: Ratings: 2 KOs before the 90-second clock. Try Belt hangs on to the edge, so go for the ones at the edge. 3 stocks each.

intro.text: Desert. A long table, a stack of scripts, and a page missing from every copy.
Table read for the Season 10 finale. The script is sealed, so tonight the cast will read the fights instead. The network wants two KOs in ninety seconds, which is what the missing page asks for.
I have read every page of the show. I have not read this one.
Nobody has.

outro.text: Strong read.
The missing page has surfaced. It has one line on it, in the Orchestrator's handwriting: the finale needs two of him.
He wrote that himself?
The network is checking.

title: Cliffhanger
tagline: The last night of the season ends the way television ends a season: mid-sentence.
hint: Quota: deal 280% before the 100-second clock runs out. Every hit lands a little harder (damage 110%). Pyro Singer sets the stage on fire, so keep moving and keep hitting.

intro.text: Cursed Town. The sky over the Foundry is a single shot held too long.
Season 9 ends on a cliffhanger. The network asks for 280 percent in a hundred seconds, and will not say what happens after. We are told there is a baton involved.
I have a song for the cliffhanger. It does not resolve.
Then sing it fast.

outro.text: To be continued.
The network has released the finale card. Two sign-up sheets, one name on both. It is the same handwriting, and nobody will say whose.
Two sheets. Fine. Same time tomorrow.
Four teasers. One cliffhanger. Two names on the sheet.
